extracted.intended_audience: Citizens of New York and the American public (readers considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution)
extracted.subtask_short: assessing republican government and Union benefits
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the merits of a republican (representative) government and a commercial/political Union versus smaller or purely democratic confederacies, focusing on faction control, commerce, naval power, and revenue. The page argues which institutional features best secure public good and private rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of faction
rubrics_metrics.description: By a faction, I understand a number of citizens, whether amounting to a majority or a minority of the whole, who are united and actuated by some common impulse of passion, or of interest, adversed to the rights of other citizens, or to the permanent and aggregate interests of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies what counts as a faction (majority or minority united by common passion/interest opposed to others' rights or public good). Use this definition as the baseline for diagnosing political groupings and dangers to public policy and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two principal cures for faction
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two methods of curing the mischiefs of faction: the one, by removing its causes; the other, by controlling its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any institutional design should consider whether it seeks to remove causes (generally infeasible or undesirable) or control effects (practical). The text argues controlling effects is the realistic objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removing causes is impracticable or worse
rubrics_metrics.description: Two methods of removing the causes of faction: the one, by destroying the liberty which is essential to its existence; the other, by giving to every citizen the same opinions, the same passions, and the same interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both proposed 'remedies' for causes are rejected: abolishing liberty is 'worse than the disease' and forcing uniformity of opinion is impracticable because reason and self-interest will always differ. Institutional prescriptions must respect liberty and human diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root causes of faction are in human nature and property
rubrics_metrics.description: The latent causes of faction are thus sown in the nature of man... The diversity in the faculties of men, from which the rights of property originate, is not less an insuperable obstacle to a uniformity of interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that factions arise from inherent differences (opinions, passions, property). Policy design should assume these causes cannot be eradicated and thus focus on mitigating their political harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control effects: prevent majority faction oppression
rubrics_metrics.description: Either the existence of the same passion or interest in a majority at the same time must be prevented, or the majority... must be rendered, by their number and local situation, unable to concert and carry into effect schemes of oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional rules should (a) avoid letting the same corrupt passion dominate a majority, or (b) structure representation and geography so a majority cannot coordinate to oppress minorities. This is the central desideratum in rescuing popular government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pure democracy cannot cure faction
rubrics_metrics.description: A pure democracy... can admit of no cure for the mischiefs of faction. A common passion or interest will... be felt by a majority of the whole... there is nothing to check the inducements to sacrifice the weaker party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct popular assemblies are especially vulnerable to majority faction; thus institutional designs that rely on direct democracy should be considered inadequate for protecting rights over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: A republic (representation) helps control factions
rubrics_metrics.description: A republic, by which I mean a government in which the scheme of representation takes place, opens a different prospect, and promises the cure for which we are seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative government 'refines and enlarges the public views' by filtering public opinion through elected representatives, making the public voice more likely to be consonant with the public good. However, beware corruption/intrigue of representatives—representation is a mitigating, not foolproof, mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two great advantages of republic over democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The two great points of difference between a democracy and a republic are: first, the delegation of the government... to a small number of citizens elected by the rest; secondly, the greater number of citizens, and greater sphere of country, over which the latter may be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional proposals by whether they (a) delegate judgment to a chosen body that can refine public views, and (b) allow a larger sphere of polity, increasing diversity and reducing the chance a single faction dominates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation improves candidate selection in larger republics
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proportion of fit characters be not less in the large than in the small republic, the former will present a greater option, and consequently a greater probability of a fit choice... it will be more difficult for unworthy candidates to practice with success the vicious arts by which elections are too often carried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger electorates increase the pool of qualified candidates and make corrupt election practices harder; evaluate representational structures for elector-to-representative ratios and vulnerability to electoral manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tradeoff: size of constituency vs local knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: By enlarging too much the number of electors, you render the representatives too little acquainted with all their local circumstances and lesser interests; as by reducing it too much, you render him unduly attached to these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should seek a mean: representatives must be numerous enough to avoid cabals but not so remote as to ignore local concerns. The federal arrangement is presented as a practical compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large republics and extended sphere reduce faction danger
rubrics_metrics.description: The smaller the society, the fewer probably will be the distinct parties and interests composing it... Extend the sphere, and you take in a greater variety of parties and interests; you make it less probable that a majority of the whole will have a common motive to invade the rights of other citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing political units, consider geographic and population scale as a tool: broader scope increases interest diversity and communication costs for conspiratorial majorities, thus protecting minority rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union (national scale) is preferable to several small confederacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Hence, it clearly appears, that the same advantage which a republic has over a democracy, in controlling the effects of faction, is enjoyed by a large over a small republic,--is enjoyed by the Union over the States composing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national Union combines the advantages of representation and scale: it expands variety of interests and erects obstacles to concerted majority oppression across the whole country; use this as a criterion when choosing between unionized or fragmented governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union strengthens commercial bargaining power
rubrics_metrics.description: If we continue united, we may counteract a policy so unfriendly to our prosperity in a variety of ways. By prohibitory regulations, extending, at the same time, throughout the States, we may oblige foreign countries to bid against each other, for the privileges of our markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate commercial policy capacity by whether the polity can act collectively (e.g., unified prohibitions or tariffs) to extract favorable concessions and leverage from foreign powers; fragmentation weakens bargaining power.

rubrics_metrics.name: A federal navy is necessary and more feasible under Union
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be no doubt that the continuance of the Union under an efficient government would put it in our power... to create a navy which... would at least be of respectable weight if thrown into the scale of either of two contending parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess national defense capacity by pooled resources: different regions provide naval stores, iron, seamen, and shipbuilding materials. A unified polity is more likely to sustain a navy than separate states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate national power needed to secure neutral rights and active commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights of neutrality will only be respected when they are defended by an adequate power. A nation, despicable by its weakness, forfeits even the privilege of being neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign respect for commerce (neutrality, protection of seaborne trade) depends on credible national power; evaluate whether political arrangements produce sufficient deterrent/defensive capacity to secure trade rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union secures shared commercial rights (fisheries, navigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are rights of great moment to the trade of America which are rights of the Union--I allude to the fisheries, to the navigation of the Western lakes, and to that of the Mississippi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies affecting common resources and navigation routes benefit from national adjudication and defense; fragmentation risks losing these rights to more powerful partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce promotes national wealth and facilitates taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosperity of commerce... has... become a primary object... By multiplying the means of gratification, by promoting the introduction and circulation of the precious metals... it serves to vivify and invigorate the channels of industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing fiscal and economic policy, prioritize commerce growth because it increases money circulation and tax capacity; commerce-driven prosperity should be a metric for evaluating economic institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary reliance on indirect taxes (imposts and excises) in America
rubrics_metrics.description: In America, it is evident that we must a long time depend for the means of revenue chiefly on such duties. In most parts of it, excises must be confined within a narrow compass... duties on imported articles form a large branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess revenue systems realistically: direct taxation is politically and practically limited in the U.S. context; therefore, duties/imposts on imports and certain excises are preferred revenue sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union makes duties more productive and collection more efficacious
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as [Union] would contribute to rendering regulations for the collection of the duties more simple and efficacious, so far it must serve to answer the purposes of making the same rate of duties more productive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A unified customs regime reduces evasion and interstate smuggling, allowing higher and more productive tariffs; evaluate customs administration by its uniformity and enforcement across the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interstate illicit trade undermines revenue without Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The relative situation of these States... all these are circumstances that would conspire to render an illicit trade between them a matter of little difficulty, and would insure frequent evasions of the commercial regulations of each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating fiscal feasibility, account for internal geography and close links among subunits that make smuggling easy; fragmentation forces lower duties and weaker enforcement to avoid evasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: American temperament resists excise-style direct enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The genius of the people will ill brook the inquisitive and peremptory spirit of excise laws... the pockets of the farmers... will reluctantly yield but scanty supplies, in the unwelcome shape of impositions on their houses and lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers should consider local political acceptability: heavy excise/direct property taxes face cultural and political resistance in the U.S., favoring less intrusive indirect taxation mechanisms.
